title.zh: 卷十四 列傳第八 江淹 任昉
title.raw: 卷十四 列傳第八 江淹 任昉 Volume 14: Jiang Yan; Ren Fang

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第十四 列傳第八

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 14, Biographies 8
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 14, Biographies 8

sentences.zh: 江淹 任昉

translations.literal: Jiang Yan; Ren Fang
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan; Ren Fang

sentences.zh: 江淹，字文通，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan, styled Wentong, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧好學，沉靜少交遊。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, poor, and fond of study, he was quiet and kept few companions.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless while young, poor but devoted to books, he lived inwardly and made few friends.

sentences.zh: 起家南徐州從事，轉奉朝請。

translations.literal: He first entered office as staff officer in South Xuzhou, then was transferred to attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a South Xuzhou staff officer, then became a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素好士，淹隨景素在南兗州。

translations.literal: Song's Prince Jing of Pingping, Jingsu, loved scholars; Yan followed Jingsu in Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Prince Jing of Pingping, Jingsu, prized men of letters; Yan served him in Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣陵令郭彥文得罪，辭連淹，繫州獄。

translations.literal: Guangling magistrate Guo Yanwen offended the law; Yan was implicated in his defense and imprisoned in the provincial jail.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling magistrate Guo Yanwen ran afoul of the law; Yan was caught up in the case and held in the provincial prison.

sentences.zh: 淹獄中上書曰：

translations.literal: In prison Yan submitted a memorial that read:
translations.idiomatic: From his cell Yan sent up a memorial, which said:

sentences.zh: 昔者，賤臣叩心，飛霜擊於燕地；

translations.literal: Of old a loyal minister beat his breast in grief until frost fell on the land of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago a loyal subject struck his heart in anguish, and frost answered on the plains of Yan;

sentences.zh: 庶女告天，振風襲於齊臺。

translations.literal: a common woman cried to Heaven until a shaking wind struck the tower of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: a common daughter cried to Heaven, and a rending wind struck the tower of Qi.

sentences.zh: 下官每讀其書，未嘗不廢卷流涕。

translations.literal: Each time your servant reads those words he cannot lay the scroll down without weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever your servant reads those lines he cannot close the book without tears.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 士有一定之論，女有不易之行。

translations.literal: A gentleman has a settled code; a woman has conduct that does not change.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman holds to a fixed standard; a woman keeps faith that will not bend.

sentences.zh: 信而見疑，貞而爲戮，是以壯夫義士伏死而不顧者此也。

translations.literal: Trusted yet suspected, loyal yet punished to death—therefore brave men and men of honor lie down to die and do not look back.
translations.idiomatic: Believed in yet doubted, steadfast yet slain—for that reason stalwarts and men of honor face death and never turn aside.

sentences.zh: 下官聞仁不可恃，善不可依，始謂徒語，乃今知之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that benevolence cannot be relied on and goodness cannot be leaned on; he once thought that mere talk, but now he knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant heard that kindness cannot be trusted and virtue cannot be depended on; he took it for empty saying—now he knows it true.

sentences.zh: 伏願大王暫停左右，少加憐鑒。

translations.literal: He bows and begs Your Highness to pause your attendants a moment and grant a little pity and clear sight.
translations.idiomatic: He bows and begs Your Highness to stay your attendants briefly and lend a measure of pity and clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 下官本蓬戶桑樞之民，布衣韋帶之士，退不飾《詩書》以驚愚，進不買名聲於天下。

translations.literal: Your servant was born a man of wicker doors and mulberry pivots, a scholar in hemp cloak and leather belt; in retreat he did not polish the Odes and Documents to startle the dull, in advance he did not buy a name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is a man of wicker doors and mulberry pivots, a common scholar in hemp and leather; he did not dress up the Odes and Documents to dazzle fools, nor purchase renown under heaven.

sentences.zh: 日者謬得升降承明之闕，出入金華之殿，何嘗不局影凝嚴，側身扃禁者乎？

translations.literal: Lately, by mistake, he was raised and lowered through the gate of Bright Hall, in and out of the Golden Flower Hall—when did he not shrink his shadow before stern guards and walk sideways past barred doors?
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago, by error, he passed the Bright Hall gate and walked the Golden Flower halls—was he not always folding his shadow before the guards and edging past the locks?

sentences.zh: 竊慕大王之義，爲門下之賓，備鳴盜淺術之餘，豫三五賤伎之末。

translations.literal: He secretly admired Your Highness's righteousness and became a guest at your gate, supplied with the leavings of shallow arts and placed among the humblest of petty skills.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly honored Your Highness's righteousness and entered your gate as a retainer, given only the dregs of shallow craft and a place among the meanest talents.

sentences.zh: 大王惠以恩光，眄以顏色。

translations.literal: Your Highness showed him favor in grace and glanced on him with a kind face.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness favored him with grace and looked on him with kindness.

sentences.zh: 實佩荊卿黃金之賜，竊感豫讓國士之分矣。

translations.literal: Truly he wore the gift of Jing Ke's yellow gold and felt in secret the bond Yu Rang owed a lord of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He truly bore the gift of Jing Ke's gold and felt in his bones the debt Yu Rang owed a lord of the land.

sentences.zh: 常欲結纓伏劍，少謝萬一，剖心摩踵，以報所天。

translations.literal: He often wished to knot his cap and lay down his sword, to repay you in the smallest measure, to split his heart and wear down his heels for the lord he served.
translations.idiomatic: He often meant to knot his cap and offer his sword, to repay you in the least part, to break his heart and grind his heels for the lord he served.

sentences.zh: 不圖小人固陋，坐貽謗缺，迹墜昭憲，身限幽圄。

translations.literal: He never thought a mean man's narrowness would seat him in slander; his steps fell from bright law, his person was shut in a dark cell.
translations.idiomatic: He never dreamed a petty man's spite would trap him in accusation; his name fell from the bright statutes, his body was caged in the black jail.

sentences.zh: 履影弔心，酸鼻痛骨。

translations.literal: He walks his shadow and mourns his heart; his nose burns sour and his bones ache.
translations.idiomatic: He treads on his shadow and weeps in his heart; acid rises in his nose and pain cuts his bones.

sentences.zh: 下官聞虧名爲辱，虧形次之，是以每一念來，忽若有遺。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that to lose one's name is disgrace and to lose one's form comes next; therefore each time the thought returns he feels as though something were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that to lose one's name is shame and to lose one's body is worse still; each time the thought returns he feels something torn away.

sentences.zh: 加以涉旬月，迫季秋，天光沉陰，左右無色。

translations.literal: Moreover he has passed a full month and reached late autumn; the sky sinks in gloom and there is no color left at his sides.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover a month has passed into late autumn; heaven hangs dark and there is no light at either hand.

sentences.zh: 身非木石，與獄吏爲伍。

translations.literal: His person is not wood or stone, yet he shares a ward with the jailers.
translations.idiomatic: He is not wood or stone, yet he keeps company with the turnkeys.

sentences.zh: 此少卿所以仰天搥心，泣盡而繼之以血者也。

translations.literal: That is why Sir Shaoqing beat his breast to Heaven, wept until he had no tears, and went on bleeding.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the Grand Historian beat his breast to Heaven, wept his eyes dry, and still shed blood.

sentences.zh: 下官雖乏鄉曲之譽，然嘗聞君子之行矣。

translations.literal: Your servant lacks the praise of his village, yet he has heard how a gentleman walks.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant lacks fame in his district, yet he has heard the gentleman's way.

sentences.zh: 其上則隱於簾肆之間，臥於巖石之下；

translations.literal: At the highest he hides between curtain and market stall or lies on stone in the hills;
translations.idiomatic: At the highest he hides behind shop curtains or sleeps on mountain stone;

sentences.zh: 次則結綬金馬之庭，高議雲臺之上；

translations.literal: next he knots his sash in the court of golden horses and speaks high doctrine on the Cloud Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: next he ties his sash in the hall of golden horses and argues great policy on the Cloud Terrace;

sentences.zh: 次則虜南越之君，繫單于之頸：俱啓丹册，並圖青史。

translations.literal: next he takes the lord of Southern Yue captive and binds the Chanyu by the neck: all open the red register and share a place in the green histories.
translations.idiomatic: next he seizes the lord of Southern Yue and collars the Chanyu: each enters the vermilion book and wins a line in the blue annals.

sentences.zh: 寧當爭分寸之末，競刀錐之利哉！

translations.literal: Would he contend for a hair's breadth or vie for the edge of a knife awl!
translations.idiomatic: Would he fight for a hair's breadth or compete for a needle's point!

sentences.zh: 然下官聞積毀銷金，積讒糜骨。

translations.literal: Yet your servant has heard that slander piled high melts gold and calumny piled high grinds bone to meal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant has heard that slander heaped high can melt gold and malice heaped high can grind bone to dust.

sentences.zh: 古則直生取疑於盜金，近則伯魚被名於不義。

translations.literal: In antiquity Straightborn was suspected for stolen gold; in recent times Boyu was stained with an unrighteous name.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Straightborn was doubted over stolen gold; in recent times Boyu was marked with an unjust name.

sentences.zh: 彼之二才，猶或如此；

translations.literal: Those two talents were treated so;
translations.idiomatic: Men of such gifts suffered thus;

sentences.zh: 況在下官，焉能自免。

translations.literal: how much more your servant—how could he escape!
translations.idiomatic: how much more your servant—how could he be spared!

sentences.zh: 昔上將之恥，絳侯幽獄；

translations.literal: Of old a great general's shame was Hong Hou in a dungeon;
translations.idiomatic: Of old a great general's shame was Hong Hou in the cells;

sentences.zh: 名臣之羞，史遷下室，如下官尚何言哉！

translations.literal: a famous minister's blush was the Historian in the lower chamber—as for your servant, what more can he say!
translations.idiomatic: a famous minister's blush was the Historian in the pit—as for your servant, what words remain!

sentences.zh: 夫魯連之智，辭祿而不反；

translations.literal: Lu Zhonglian was wise yet declined salary and never returned;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhonglian had wisdom yet refused rank and never came back;

sentences.zh: 接輿之賢，行歌而忘歸。

translations.literal: Jieyu was worthy yet walked singing and forgot to go home.
translations.idiomatic: Jieyu had worth yet sang as he walked and forgot the homeward road.

sentences.zh: 子陵閉關於東越，仲蔚杜門於西秦，亦良可知也。

translations.literal: Yan Ziling shut his gate in Eastern Yue and Zhong Wei barred his door in Western Qin—the lesson is plain enough.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ziling closed his door in Eastern Yue and Zhong Wei sealed his gate in Western Qin—the meaning is clear enough.

sentences.zh: 若使下官事非其虛，罪得其實，亦當鉗口吞舌，伏匕首以殞身，何以見齊魯奇節之人，燕趙悲歌之士乎？

translations.literal: If your servant's affair were not empty and his guilt were real, he should clamp his mouth, swallow his tongue, and fall on a dagger—why should he face the strange integrity of Qi and Lu or the grieving singers of Yan and Zhao!
translations.idiomatic: If your servant's charge were true and his guilt solid, he should seal his mouth, swallow his tongue, and die on a blade—why meet the strange honor of Qi and Lu or the mourning singers of Yan and Zhao!

sentences.zh: 方今聖曆欽明，天下樂業，青雲浮雒，榮光塞河。

translations.literal: Now the holy calendar is revered and bright; the realm rejoices in its work; azure clouds float over the Luo, glory fills the river.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred reign is revered and bright; all under heaven delights in its labor; azure clouds drift above the Luo, splendor blocks the river.

sentences.zh: 西洎臨洮、狄道，北距飛狐、陽原，莫不浸仁沐義，照景飲醴。

translations.literal: West to Lintao and Didao, north to Flying Fox and Yangyuan—none but is steeped in benevolence, bathed in righteousness, warmed by the sun, drinking the sweet wine.
translations.idiomatic: West to Lintao and Didao, north to Flying Fox and Yangyuan—every land is steeped in kindness, washed in duty, lit by the sun, drinking the sweet cup.

sentences.zh: 而下官抱痛圜門，含憤獄戶，一物之微，有足悲者。

translations.literal: Yet your servant embraces pain at the round gate and holds wrath in the prison door; the slightest thing is enough to grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant nurses pain at the round gate and hoards rage in the jail— the smallest matter is cause for grief.

sentences.zh: 仰惟大王少垂明白，則梧丘之魂，不愧於沉首；

translations.literal: He looks up and begs Your Highness to bend a little clear light; then the soul at Wuzhu Mound need not blush for a head sunk in earth;
translations.idiomatic: He looks up and begs Your Highness to grant a little clear sight; then the shade at Wuzhu Mound need not blush for a buried head;

sentences.zh: 鵠亭之鬼，無恨於灰骨。

translations.literal: the ghost at Goose Pavilion need not regret bones turned to ash.
translations.idiomatic: the ghost at Goose Pavilion need not regret bones burned to ash.

sentences.zh: 不任肝膽之切，敬因執事以聞。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the cut of liver and gall, he respectfully sends word through your attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the cut of heart and liver, he respectfully reports through your officers.

sentences.zh: 此心旣照，死且不朽。

translations.literal: Once this heart is seen, death itself will not perish.
translations.idiomatic: Once this heart is known, even death will not die.

sentences.zh: 景素覽書，卽日出之。

translations.literal: Jingsu read the memorial and released him that same day.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu read the letter and freed him the same day.

sentences.zh: 尋舉南徐州秀才，對策上第，轉巴陵王國左常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was nominated South Xuzhou village scholar; in the policy examination he placed first and was made left regular attendant of the Prince of Baling's state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recommended as South Xuzhou village scholar, topped the policy exam, and became left regular attendant in the Prince of Baling's household.

sentences.zh: 景素爲荊州，淹從之鎮。

translations.literal: When Jingsu went to Jing province, Yan followed him to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingsu took Jing province, Yan went with him to the command.

sentences.zh: 少帝卽位，多失德。

translations.literal: When the Depraved Emperor succeeded, he lost virtue in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: When the Depraved Emperor took the throne, his conduct failed in many ways.

sentences.zh: 景素專據上流，咸勸因此舉事。

translations.literal: Jingsu held the upper reaches exclusively; many urged him to raise arms on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu held the upper river country alone; many urged him to strike while he could.

sentences.zh: 淹每從容諫曰：「流言納禍，二叔所以同亡；

translations.literal: Yan often remonstrated at leisure: "Slander brings disaster in—
translations.idiomatic: Yan often urged him gently: "Rumor draws ruin—

sentences.zh: 抵局銜怨，七國於焉俱斃。

translations.literal: that is why the Two Uncles perished together; nursing a grudge at the chessboard—
translations.idiomatic: that is how the Two Uncles died as one; nursing a grudge at the board—

sentences.zh: 殿下不求宗廟之安，而信左右之計，則復見麋鹿霜露棲於姑蘇之臺矣。

translations.literal: that is why the Seven States all fell. Your Highness does not seek the peace of the ancestral temples but trusts the counsel of those at your side; then you will again see deer in frost and dew lodging on the Terrace of Gusu."
translations.idiomatic: that is how the Seven States were destroyed. Your Highness does not seek the altars' safety but trusts men at your ear; then you will again see deer in frost and dew on the Terrace of Gusu."

sentences.zh: 」景素不納。

translations.literal: Jingsu did not accept his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及鎮京口，淹又爲鎮軍參軍事，領南東海郡丞。

translations.literal: When he garrisoned Jingkou, Yan was again made staff officer to the Pacifying Army and concurrently magistrate of Southern Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When he held Jingkou, Yan became pacifying-army staff officer and also magistrate of Southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 景素與腹心日夜謀議，淹知禍機將發，乃贈詩十五首以諷焉。

translations.literal: Jingsu and his intimates plotted day and night; Yan saw ruin coming and sent fifteen poems as indirect warning.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu and his inner circle schemed night and day; Yan saw disaster near and offered fifteen poems as warning.

sentences.zh: 會南東海太守陸澄丁艱，淹自謂郡丞應行郡事，景素用司馬柳世隆。

translations.literal: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng entered mourning for his father, Yan thought that as commandery aide he should act as prefect; Jingsu appointed staff officer Liu Shilong instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Donghai prefect Lu Cheng began mourning, Yan assumed the aide should run the commandery; Jingsu gave the post to staff officer Liu Shilong.

sentences.zh: 淹固求之，景素大怒，言於選部，黜爲建安吳興令。

translations.literal: Yan pressed his claim; Jingsu was furious and spoke to the selection office, demoting him to magistrate of Jian'an in Wu-xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan insisted; Jingsu raged, spoke to personnel, and demoted him to Jian'an magistrate in Wu-xing.

sentences.zh: 淹在縣三年。

translations.literal: Yan held the district three years.
translations.idiomatic: Yan served in the county three years.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，齊帝輔政，聞其才，召爲尚書駕部郎、驃騎參軍事。

translations.literal: At the start of the Ascendant Bright era, when Qi's emperor held regency, he heard of Yan's talent and summoned him as Masters of Writing director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Ascendant Bright, with Qi's emperor as regent, he heard of Yan and made him secretariat director of the imperial equipage and valiant-cavalry staff officer.

sentences.zh: 俄而荊州刺史沈攸之作亂，高帝謂淹曰：「天下紛紛若是，君謂何如？

translations.literal: Before long Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rebelled; Gaodi said to Yan, "The realm is in such turmoil—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing inspector Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Gaodi asked Yan, "The world is chaos like this—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」淹對曰：「昔項強而劉弱，袁衆而曹寡，羽號令諸侯，卒受一劍之辱，紹跨躡四州，終爲奔北之虜。

translations.literal: Yan answered, "Of old Xiang was strong and Liu weak, Yuan had many men and Cao few; Yu commanded the feudal lords yet in the end suffered the shame of a single sword, Yuan straddled four provinces yet ended a fugitive north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered, "Once Xiang Yu was strong and Liu Bang weak, Yuan Shao had numbers and Cao Cao few; Yu ruled the lords yet died by one sword, Yuan held four provinces yet fled north in defeat.

sentences.zh: 此謂『在德不在鼎』。

translations.literal: This is what they call 'virtue, not the vessel.'
translations.idiomatic: That is what men mean by 'power lies in virtue, not in the tripod.'

sentences.zh: 公何疑哉？

translations.literal: Why should you doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: What doubt remains for you?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「聞此言者多矣，試爲慮之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Many have spoken so—try to think it through."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Many say the same—work it through for me."

sentences.zh: 」淹曰：「公雄武有奇略，一勝也；

translations.literal: Yan said, "Your Lordship is boldly martial with a strange design—one victory;
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "You are boldly martial with a singular plan—first victory;

sentences.zh: 寬容而仁恕，二勝也；

translations.literal: tolerant and humane—two victories;
translations.idiomatic: tolerant and humane—second victory;

sentences.zh: 賢能畢力，三勝也；

translations.literal: the worthy exert all their strength—three victories;
translations.idiomatic: the worthy give all their strength—third victory;

sentences.zh: 民望所歸，四勝也；

translations.literal: the people's hopes turn to you—four victories;
translations.idiomatic: the people's hopes rest on you—fourth victory;

sentences.zh: 奉天子而伐叛逆，五勝也。

translations.literal: you hold the Son of Heaven and strike the rebel—five victories.
translations.idiomatic: you hold the Son of Heaven and punish rebellion—fifth victory.

sentences.zh: 彼志銳而器小，一敗也；

translations.literal: Their will is sharp but their vessel small—one defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Their will is keen but their measure small—first defeat;

sentences.zh: 有威而無恩，二敗也；

translations.literal: they have awe but no grace—two defeats;
translations.idiomatic: they inspire fear but grant no grace—second defeat;

sentences.zh: 士卒解體，三敗也；

translations.literal: their soldiers are loosened—three defeats;
translations.idiomatic: their troops are slack—third defeat;

sentences.zh: 搢紳不懷，四敗也；

translations.literal: the gentry do not cling to them—four defeats;
translations.idiomatic: the gentry do not stand with them—fourth defeat;

sentences.zh: 懸兵數千里，而無同惡相濟，五敗也。

translations.literal: they hang their army a thousand li away with none of like mind to aid them—five defeats.
translations.idiomatic: they stretch an army a thousand li with no ally of one heart—fifth defeat.

sentences.zh: 故雖豺狼十萬，而終爲我獲焉。

translations.literal: Though they have a hundred thousand wolves, in the end they will be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Though jackals number in the tens of thousands, in the end they are yours."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「君談過矣。

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "You talk too much."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "You overspeak."

sentences.zh: 」是時軍書表記，皆使淹具草。

translations.literal: At that time military reports and memorials were all drafted by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In those days every army dispatch and memorial passed through Yan's hand.

sentences.zh: 相國建，補記室參軍事。

translations.literal: When the chief minister's office was established, he was made record-keeper staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister's office was set up, he became record-keeper on the staff.

sentences.zh: 建元初，又爲驃騎豫章王記室，帶東武令，參掌詔册，並典國史。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, with concurrent magistrate of Dongwu, charged with edicts and patents and also keeper of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyuan's opening he was again valiant-cavalry record-keeper to the Prince of Yuzhang, magistrate of Dongwu in addition, drafting edicts and patents and tending the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永明初，遷驍騎將軍，掌國史。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongming he was made Valiant Cavalry General and kept charge of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongming's opening he became valiant cavalry general and still held the national history.

sentences.zh: 出爲建武將軍、廬陵內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Martial Glory and interior magistrate of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as general who establishes martial glory and Luling interior magistrate.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，還爲驍騎將軍，兼尚書左丞，尋復以本官領國子博士。

translations.literal: After three years in office he returned as Valiant Cavalry General and concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he again held his former post with charge as Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he returned as valiant cavalry general and vice director of the masters of writing; soon he held the same rank and led the national university as erudite.

sentences.zh: 少帝初，以本官兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the start of the Depraved Emperor's reign he held his former post with concurrent Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Depraved Emperor began his reign Yan kept his rank and also served as censor.

sentences.zh: 時明帝作相，因謂淹曰：「君昔在尚書中，非公事不妄行，在官寬猛能折衷；

translations.literal: Mingdi was then chief minister and said to Yan, "When you were in the Masters of Writing you never acted without public cause; in office you balanced lenity and severity;
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi was regent and told Yan, "In the secretariat you never moved without public business; in office you could balance mercy and severity;

sentences.zh: 今爲南司，足以震肅百僚。

translations.literal: now as southern inspector you are enough to awe and sober the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: now as southern inspector you can shake the hundred officials sober."

sentences.zh: 」淹答曰：「今日之事，可謂當官而行，更恐才劣志薄，不足以仰稱明旨耳。

translations.literal: Yan answered, "Today's task may be called doing the office as it demands; I only fear talent too slight and will too thin to rise to your bright intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yan answered, "Today's charge is to act as the post requires; I only fear my gift is small and my resolve thin for your clear command."

sentences.zh: 」於是彈中書令謝朏，司徒左長史王繢、護軍長史庾弘遠，並以久疾不預山陵公事；

translations.literal: Thereupon he impeached Secretariat Director Xie Tiao, Left Chief of Staff to the Minister of Education Wang Ji, and Protecting Army Chief Clerk Yu Hongyuan—all for long illness and failure to attend the mountain tomb rites;
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached secretariat director Xie Tiao, minister of education left chief of staff Wang Ji, and protecting-army chief clerk Yu Hongyuan—for long illness and absence from the imperial tomb rites;

sentences.zh: 又奏前益州刺史劉悛、梁州刺史陰智伯，並贓貨巨萬，輒收付廷尉治罪。

translations.literal: he also memorialized against former Yi province inspector Liu Jun and former Liang inspector Yin Zhibo, both for accepting bribes in the tens of thousands, and had them taken at once to the Court for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: he also charged former Yi inspector Liu Jun and former Liang inspector Yin Zhibo with bribes in the tens of thousands and sent them straight to the court for judgment.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略、永嘉太守庾曇隆，及諸郡二千石幷大縣官長，多被劾治，內外肅然。

translations.literal: Linhai prefect Shen Zhaolue, Yongjia prefect Yu Tanlong, and magistrates of two thousand bushels in many commanderies and great counties were largely impeached and disciplined; within and without the court grew stern.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai prefect Shen Zhaolue, Yongjia prefect Yu Tanlong, and many two-thousand-bushel magistrates in great districts were impeached and punished; inside and outside the court turned severe.

sentences.zh: 明帝謂淹曰：「宋世以來，不復有嚴明中丞，君今日可謂近世獨步。」

translations.literal: Mingdi said to Yan, "Since Song times there has been no stern censor like you; today you may be called unmatched in recent generations."
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi told Yan, "Since the Song there has been no censor this stern; you may be called alone in our age."

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，爲車騎臨海王長史。

translations.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, Yan was made chief of staff to the Valiant Cavalry Prince of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi succeeded, Yan became chief of staff to the valiant-cavalry prince of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 俄除廷尉卿，加給事中，遷冠軍長史，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Court Commandant with additional appointment as Supplicator, then champion chief of staff with additional appointment as Assistant State General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was court commandant and supplicator in addition, then champion chief of staff and assistant state general.

sentences.zh: 出爲宣城太守，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He went out as Xuan prefect with his general's rank unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Xuancheng prefect, general's rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 在郡四年，還爲黃門侍郎、領步兵校尉，尋爲秘書監。

translations.literal: After four years in the commandery he returned as Yellow Gate Gentleman, concurrently Infantry Colonel, soon made Palace Library Director.
translations.idiomatic: Four years in office, then back to court as yellow-gate gentleman and infantry colonel, soon keeper of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 永元中，崔慧景舉兵圍京城，衣冠悉投名刺，淹稱疾不往。

translations.literal: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing raised troops and besieged the capital; officials all sent calling cards—Yan claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan, Cui Huijing besieged the capital; every gentleman sent his card, but Yan pleaded sickness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 及事平，世服其先見。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, the age admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When the storm passed, the world praised his foresight.

sentences.zh: 淹少以文章顯，晚節才思微退，時人皆謂之才盡。

translations.literal: Yan had been famed early for writing; in his late years his talent waned—the age said his talent was spent.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen on his pen, yet in old age his gift thinned; men said his talent was spent.

sentences.zh: 凡所著述百餘篇，自撰爲前後集，幷《齊史》十志，並行於世。

translations.literal: All his writings exceeded a hundred pieces; he compiled front and rear collections himself, together with the Ten Annals of Qi History, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a hundred works, front and rear collections of his own, and the Ten Annals of Qi—all still in the world.

sentences.zh: 子蒍襲封嗣，自丹陽尹丞爲長城令，有罪削爵。

translations.literal: His son Qian inherited the fief; from Assistant to the Danyang Intendant he became magistrate of Changcheng; for a crime his noble rank was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian took the title, rose from Danyang aide to magistrate of Changcheng, then lost the fief for a crime.

sentences.zh: 普通四年，高祖追念淹功，復封蒍吳昌伯，邑如先。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Putong, Gaozu recalled Yan's merit and re-enfeoffed Qian as Marquis of Wuchang, fief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year 4 Gaozu remembered Yan's service and made Qian marquis of Wuchang again, with the old fief.

sentences.zh: 任昉，字彥昇，樂安博昌人，漢御史大夫敖之後也。

translations.literal: Ren Fang, styled Yansheng, was a native of Bochang in Le'an, descendant of the Han Censor-in-Chief Ao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang, styled Yansheng, came from Bochang in Le'an—a line from Han's censor-in-chief Ao.

sentences.zh: 父遙，齊中散大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yao was Qi Central Regular Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yao was Qi's central regular grandee.

sentences.zh: 遙妻裴氏，嘗晝寢，夢有彩旗蓋四角懸鈴，自天而墜，其一鈴落入裴懷中，心悸動，旣而有娠，生昉。

translations.literal: Yao's wife Lady Pei once slept by day and dreamed of a colored banner-canopy with bells hung at four corners, falling from heaven; one bell dropped into Pei's bosom—her heart leapt—and thereafter she conceived and bore Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's wife, Lady Pei, napped and dreamed of a colored canopy with bells at four corners falling from heaven; one bell struck her breast, her heart leapt, and soon she bore Fang.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺五寸。

translations.literal: His height was seven chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi five cun tall.

sentences.zh: 幼而好學，早知名。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning and was early renowned.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he loved books and was known early.

sentences.zh: 宋丹陽尹劉秉辟爲主簿。

translations.literal: Song Danyang Intendant Liu Bing recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bing, Song's Danyang intendant, took him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時昉年十六，以氣忤秉子。

translations.literal: Fang was then sixteen and offended Bing's son with his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was sixteen and crossed Bing's son with his pride.

sentences.zh: 久之，爲奉朝請，舉兗州秀才，拜太常博士，遷征北行參軍。

translations.literal: After some time he became Court Attendant, was recommended as Yanzhou Outstanding Talent, appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies academician, promoted to Staff Officer on the Northern Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became court attendant, was named Yanzhou outstanding talent, made a ritual academician, then staff officer on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 永明初，衛將軍王儉領丹陽尹，復引爲主簿。

translations.literal: Early Yongming, General of the Guards Wang Jian took Danyang as intendant and again recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming, Wang Jian of the guards, as Danyang intendant, drew him back as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 儉雅欽重昉，以爲當時無輩。

translations.literal: Jian deeply admired Fang and thought there was no equal in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jian prized him deeply and said no man of the time matched him.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒刑獄參軍事，入爲尚書殿中郎，轉司徒竟陵王記室參軍，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: Promoted to Criminal Office Prison staff officer, entered as Attendant of the Palace Department in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Staff Officer and Recorder to the Prince of Jingling of the Secretariat, left office for father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prison staff in the criminal office, then palace attendant in the secretariat, then recorder to the Prince of Jingling, and left for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: By nature most filial; in mourning he observed every rite.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial to the bone; in mourning he kept every rite.

sentences.zh: 服闋，續遭母憂，常廬于墓側，哭泣之地，草爲不生。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again suffered mother's mourning; he often lodged beside the tomb—in the place of his weeping grass would not grow.
translations.idiomatic: When that mourning ended, his mother died; he kept a hut by the grave, and where he wept the grass would not grow.

sentences.zh: 服除，拜太子步兵校尉、管東宮書記。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, appointed Heir Apparent Infantry Colonel, in charge of Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was heir-apparent infantry colonel, keeper of the eastern palace papers.

sentences.zh: 初，齊明帝旣廢郁林王，始爲侍中、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書事，封宣城郡公，加兵五千，使昉具表草。

translations.literal: Early, after Qi Emperor Ming had deposed the Emperor of Lin, he first became Attendant, Palace Library Director, General of Agile Cavalry with full staff equal to the Three Ministries, Yangzhou Inspector, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng with five thousand additional troops, and had Fang draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi's Emperor Ming deposed the Emperor of Lin, he first took attendant, palace library director, agile-cavalry general with full staff, Yangzhou inspector, and recorder of the secretariat, was made duke of Xuancheng with five thousand more troops, and had Fang draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：「臣本庸才，智力淺短。

translations.literal: Its words say: "Your servant is by nature mediocre, shallow in mind and short in strength.
translations.idiomatic: It runs: "Your servant is a mediocrity, shallow in wit and short in strength.

sentences.zh: 太祖高皇帝篤猶子之愛，降家人之慈；

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao cherished the love due a nephew-son and granted the kindness shown within a household;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Gao cherished a nephew as a son and gave the kindness of kin under one roof;

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝情等布衣，寄深同氣。

translations.literal: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as a commoner's equal and entrusted him with the bond of shared blood.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Emperor Wu treated him as an equal of the robe and bound him with shared blood.

sentences.zh: 武皇大漸，實奉詔言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu fell gravely ill, I truly received his charge in words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu lay dying, I truly received his charge in words.

sentences.zh: 雖自見之明，庸近所蔽，愚夫一至，偶識量己，實不忍自固於綴衣之辰，拒違於玉幾之側，遂荷顧托，導揚末命。

translations.literal: Though I saw my own light, the near and mean blinded me—yet when a fool arrives once, he happens to know his measure—and I truly could not steel myself at the hour of the embroidered robe nor refuse at the jade throne's side; thus I bore the entrustment and led the command of the final charge.
translations.idiomatic: Though I saw my own light, the near blinded me—yet even a fool, once, may know his measure—and I could not harden myself at the hour of mourning dress nor turn away beside the jade throne; so I bore the trust and carried out the last command.

sentences.zh: 雖嗣君棄常，獲罪宣德，王室不造，職臣之由。

translations.literal: Though the successor prince abandoned the norm and was condemned to uphold virtue, the royal house was undone—the fault lies with ministers like me.
translations.idiomatic: Though the heir abandoned the norm and was judged for upholding virtue, the royal house was broken—and the fault is mine.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 親則東牟，任惟博陸，徒懷子孟社稷之對，何救昌邑爭臣之譏。

translations.literal: Kinship was Eastern Mou's, the charge was Bolu's—he only harbored Zimeng's reply for state and altar, how could he save Changyi from the censure of contentious ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Kin was the Prince of Eastern Mou, the charge was Bolu's—he only kept Zimeng's answer for throne and altar; how could he spare Changyi the rebuke of contentious ministers?

sentences.zh: 四海之議，於何逃責？

translations.literal: The opinion of the four seas—how escape blame?
translations.idiomatic: The judgment of the four seas—how shall I escape blame?

sentences.zh: 陵土未乾，訓誓在耳，家國之事，一至於斯，非臣之尤，誰任其咎！

translations.literal: The imperial tomb not yet dry, instructions and warnings still in the ear—the affair of house and state has come to this; if not my fault, who bears the blame!
translations.idiomatic: The imperial tomb is not yet dry, the charge still rings in the ear—house and state have come to this; if not my fault, whose is it?

sentences.zh: 將何以肅拜高寢，虔奉武園？

translations.literal: How shall I reverently bow at the high inner chamber and devoutly serve the martial park?
translations.idiomatic: How shall I bow at the high inner chamber and serve the martial park with devotion?

sentences.zh: 悼心失圖，泣血待旦。

translations.literal: A grieving heart loses its plan; I wait for dawn weeping blood.
translations.idiomatic: A grieving heart has lost its map; I wait for dawn in tears of blood.

sentences.zh: 寧容復徼榮於家恥，宴安於國危。

translations.literal: How can I again seek glory atop family shame and feast in ease amid national peril?
translations.idiomatic: How can I again seek glory on family shame and feast while the state is in peril?

sentences.zh: 驃騎上將之元勳，神州儀刑之列岳，尚書是稱司會，中書實管王言。

translations.literal: The founding merit of the General of Agile Cavalry, the exemplar of the divine land's model lords—the Masters of Writing is called steward of assemblies, the Secretariat truly governs the king's words.
translations.idiomatic: The founding merit of the agile-cavalry general, the model lord of the divine land—the secretariat is called steward of assemblies, the palace director truly holds the king's words.

sentences.zh: 且虛飾寵章，委成禦侮，臣知不愜，物誰謂宜。

translations.literal: Yet empty ornaments of favor, entrusting defense of insult—I know it does not satisfy; who of things would say it is fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Yet empty ornaments of favor, entrusting the ward of insult—I know it will not satisfy; who would call it fitting?

sentences.zh: 但命輕鴻毛，責重山岳，存沒同歸，毀譽一貫。

translations.literal: But life is lighter than a goose feather, duty heavier than mountains; alive or dead we return together, ruin and praise one strand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet life is lighter than a goose feather and duty heavier than mountains; alive or dead we go together, ruin and praise one thread.

sentences.zh: 辭一官不減身累，增一職已黷朝經。

translations.literal: To refuse one office does not lessen the body's burden; to add one post already stains the court's rule.
translations.idiomatic: To refuse one office does not lighten the body's load; to add one post already stains the court's rule.

sentences.zh: 便當自同體國，不爲飾讓。

translations.literal: I should then be of one body with the state and not make a show of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: I should then be one body with the state and not make a show of yielding.

sentences.zh: 至於功均一匡，賞同千室，光宅近甸，奄有全邦，殞越爲期，不敢聞命，亦願曲留降鑒，卽垂聽許。

translations.literal: As for merit equal to one rectification and reward like a thousand households, shining over the nearby suburbs, covering the whole realm—for the term of my life I dare not hear the command; yet I also beg you bend your lowered discernment and grant hearing at once.
translations.idiomatic: As for merit like one rectification and reward like a thousand households, shining over the nearby suburbs and holding the whole realm—for my life's term I dare not hear the command; yet I beg you bend your lowered gaze and grant it at once.

sentences.zh: 鉅平之懇誠必固，永昌之丹慊獲申，乃知君臣之道，綽有餘裕，苟曰易昭，敢守難奪。

translations.literal: Juping's earnest plea must stand firm, Yongchang's cinnabar loyalty may be declared—then one knows the way of ruler and minister has ample surplus; if you say change is manifest, I dare keep what is hard to wrest away.
translations.idiomatic: Juping's earnest plea must stand, Yongchang's cinnabar heart may be declared—then one knows the way of ruler and minister still has room; if change is plain, I dare keep what is hard to take.

sentences.zh: 」帝惡其辭斥，甚慍，昉由是終建武中，位不過列校。

translations.literal: The emperor hated that his words rebuked him, was greatly angered—Fang from this for the whole Jianwu period never rose beyond colonel rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated the rebuke in his words and was furious; from this Fang through all Jianwu never rose above colonel.

sentences.zh: 昉雅善屬文，尤長載筆，才思無窮，當世王公表奏，莫不請焉。

translations.literal: Fang by nature excelled at composing prose, especially at wielding the brush; his talent never ceased—for that age kings and dukes' memorials, none did not ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang excelled at prose, especially at the brush; his talent never ran dry—every king and duke of the age asked him for memorials.

sentences.zh: 昉起草卽成，不加點竄。

translations.literal: Fang's drafts were finished at once, without a dot or stroke changed.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's drafts were done at once, without a dot changed.

sentences.zh: 沈約一代詞宗，深所推挹。

translations.literal: Shen Yue, master of a generation's words, deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yue, master of the age's words, prized him deeply.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died he was made secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永元末，爲司徒右長史。

translations.literal: At Yongyuan's end, became Right Chief of Staff of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan's end he was right chief of staff of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高祖克京邑，霸府初開，以昉爲驃騎記室參軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the capital, as the hegemon's office first opened, Fang was made Staff Officer and Recorder to the General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the capital and the hegemon's office opened, Fang was staff officer and recorder to the agile-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 始高祖與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿爲記室。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's Western Residence, he said with ease: "When I rise to the three offices, I shall make you my recorder."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's western residence, he said lightly, "When I reach the three offices, you shall be my recorder."

sentences.zh: 」昉亦戲高祖曰：「我若登三事，當以卿爲騎兵。

translations.literal: Fang also joked to Gaozu: "If I rise to the three ministries, I shall make you my cavalry officer."
translations.idiomatic: Fang joked back, "If I reach the three ministries, you shall be my cavalry officer."

sentences.zh: 」謂高祖善騎也。

translations.literal: Meaning Gaozu was skilled at riding.
translations.idiomatic: He meant Gaozu rode well.

sentences.zh: 至是故引昉，符昔言焉。

translations.literal: Now therefore he drew Fang in—matching the old words.
translations.idiomatic: Now he drew Fang in—keeping the old jest.

sentences.zh: 昉奉牋曰：「伏承以今月令辰，肅膺典策，德顯功高，光副四海，含生之倫，庇身有地；

translations.literal: Fang submitted a letter saying: "I humbly receive that on this month's appointed day you solemnly accept the canonical charter—virtue manifest, merit high, light paired with the four seas; every class that lives has ground to shelter its body;
translations.idiomatic: Fang submitted a letter: "I humbly receive that on this appointed day you solemnly take the canonical charter—virtue bright, merit high, light over the four seas; every living kind has ground to shelter its body;

sentences.zh: 況昉受教君子，將二十年，咳唾爲恩，眄睞成飾，小人懷惠，顧知死所。

translations.literal: As for Fang, he received a gentleman's teaching for nearly twenty years—cough and spit were grace, a glance became ornament; the small man cherishing favor knows where to die.
translations.idiomatic: As for Fang, I have received a gentleman's teaching nearly twenty years—cough and spit were grace, a glance was ornament; the small man who cherishes favor knows where to die.

sentences.zh: 昔承清宴，屬有緒言，提挈之旨，形乎善謔，豈謂多幸，斯言不渝。

translations.literal: Once at a clear banquet there was a thread of words—its lift and carry shaped in friendly jest; who thought such fortune—those words unfailing.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a clear banquet there was a thread of words, shaped in friendly jest; who thought such fortune—that those words would hold.

sentences.zh: 雖情謬先覺，而迹淪驕餌，湯沐具而非弔，大廈構而相驩。

translations.literal: Though feeling erred in foresight, traces fell among proud bait—bath and wash were ready yet no condolence, the great hall was built yet we rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: Though feeling erred in foresight, my tracks fell among proud bait—bath and wash stood ready yet no condolence came, the great hall was built yet we rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 明公道冠二儀，勳超邃古，將使伊周奉轡，桓文扶轂，神功無紀，化物何稱。

translations.literal: My lord's Way crowns the Two Principles, merit surpasses the deepest past—he will make Yi and Zhou hold the reins, Huan and Wen steady the wheels; divine work beyond record, transforming beings beyond name.
translations.idiomatic: My lord's Way crowns the two principles, merit passes the deepest past—you will make Yi and Zhou hold the reins, Huan and Wen steady the wheels; divine work beyond record, transforming beings beyond name.

sentences.zh: 府朝初建，俊賢驤首，惟此魚目，唐突璵璠。

translations.literal: As the office first rose, worthy men tossed their heads—only this fish's eye carelessly bumped the jade of pearls.
translations.idiomatic: As the office first rose, worthy men tossed their heads—only this fish's eye bumped the pearl jade by mistake.

sentences.zh: 顧己循涯，𢉴知塵忝，千載一逢，再造難答。

translations.literal: Looking back at my own bank, I know how dust clings to the frontier—a meeting once in a thousand ages, a rebirth hard to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at my own bank, I know how dust stains the frontier—a meeting once in a thousand ages, a rebirth hard to repay.

sentences.zh: 雖則殞越，且知非報。」

translations.literal: Though I will overstep and die, I know it is not repayment."
translations.idiomatic: Though I overstep and die, I know it is not repayment."

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，禪讓文誥，多昉所具。

translations.literal: When the Liang terrace was raised, the abdication documents were mostly Fang's work.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang terrace rose, the abdication documents were mostly Fang's work.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，拜黃門侍郎，遷吏部郎中，尋以本官掌著作。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman, promoted to Personnel Section Director, soon in that office he also supervised the Compilation Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was yellow-gate gentleman, then personnel section director, soon in that post supervising the compilation office as well.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，出爲義興太守。

translations.literal: Tianjian year 2, went out as Administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 2 he went out as administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 在任清潔，兒妾食麥而已。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and austere—concubines and sons ate only wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was pure and spare—concubines and sons ate only wheat.

sentences.zh: 友人彭城到溉，溉弟洽，從昉共爲山澤遊。

translations.literal: His friend Dao Gai of Pengcheng—Gai's younger brother He—had roamed mountains and streams with Fang.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Dao Gai of Pengcheng—Gai's younger brother He—had roamed mountains and streams with him.

sentences.zh: 及被代登舟，止有米五斛。

translations.literal: When replaced and boarding the boat, he had only five hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: When he was replaced and boarded the boat, he had only five hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 旣至無衣，鎮軍將軍沈約遣裙衫迎之。

translations.literal: On arrival he had no clothes; Suppressing Army General Shen Yue sent skirt and robe to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he had no clothes; Shen Yue the suppressing-army general sent skirt and robe to meet him.

sentences.zh: 重除吏部郎中，參掌大選，居職不稱。

translations.literal: Again appointed Personnel Section Director, assisted in great selections—in the post he did not excel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again personnel section director, helping with great selections—in the post he did not excel.

sentences.zh: 尋轉御史中丞，秘書監，領前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Censor-in-Chief, Palace Library Director, concurrently Front Army General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was censor-in-chief, palace library director, and front army general together.

sentences.zh: 自齊永元以來，秘閣四部，篇卷紛雜，昉手自讎校，由是篇目定焉。

translations.literal: Since Qi Yongyuan, the four sections of the secret library had tangled rolls—Fang collated them by hand, and thereby the catalog was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qi's Yongyuan the secret library's four sections were tangled—Fang collated them by hand, and the catalog was fixed.

sentences.zh: 六年春，出爲寧朔將軍、新安太守。

translations.literal: Sixth year spring, went out as Pacify-the-North General, Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year's spring he went out as pacify-the-north general and administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 在郡不事邊幅，率然曳杖，徒行邑郭，民通辭訟者，就路決焉。

translations.literal: In the commandery he did not trouble about dress; simply trailing his staff, he walked the town on foot—people bringing suits and pleas, he judged on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he did not trouble about dress; staff in hand, he walked the town on foot—whoever brought suit or plea, he judged on the road.

sentences.zh: 爲政清省，吏民便之。

translations.literal: His governance was pure and spare; officials and people found it easy.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was pure and spare; officials and people found it easy.

sentences.zh: 視事朞歲，卒於官舍，時年四十九。

translations.literal: After a full year in office, he died in the government house, age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year in office he died in the government house, at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 闔境痛惜，百姓共立祠堂於城南。

translations.literal: The whole territory grieved; the people together built a shrine south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The whole territory grieved; the people together built a shrine south of the city.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞問，卽日舉哀，哭之甚慟。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard, that very day he held mourning and wept with extreme grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, that very day he mourned and wept with extreme grief.

sentences.zh: 追贈太常卿，諡曰敬子。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Ceremonies, posthumous title Jingzi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand master of ceremonies, posthumous title Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 昉好交結，獎進士友，得其延譽者，率多升擢，故衣冠貴遊，莫不爭與交好，坐上賓客，恒有數十。

translations.literal: Fang loved to bind friendships and encourage scholar friends—those who gained his praise mostly rose in rank; thus the gentry and nobles all vied to befriend him; guests at his seat were always several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Fang loved friendship and lifted scholar friends—those who won his praise mostly rose; so gentry and nobles all vied to know him, and guests at his seat were always several tens.

sentences.zh: 時人慕之，號曰任君，言如漢之三君也。

translations.literal: Men of the age admired this and called him Lord Ren—meaning like the Three Lords of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the age admired this and called him Lord Ren—as with the Three Lords of Han.

sentences.zh: 陳郡殷芸與建安太守到溉書曰：「哲人云亡，儀表長謝。

translations.literal: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to Administrator of Jian'an Dao Gai: "The wise man has passed; the compass fails.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yun of Chen commandery wrote to Dao Gai, administrator of Jian'an: "The wise man has passed; the compass fails.

sentences.zh: 元龜何寄？

translations.literal: To whom does the divine tortoise belong?
translations.idiomatic: To whom does the divine tortoise belong?

sentences.zh: 指南誰託？

translations.literal: Who will carry the lodestone?"
translations.idiomatic: Who will carry the lodestone?"

sentences.zh: 」其爲士友所推如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he pushed by gentlemen friends.
translations.idiomatic: Thus gentlemen friends pushed him.

sentences.zh: 昉不治生產，至乃居無室宅。

translations.literal: Fang did not manage livelihood—so much so that he had no dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Fang did not manage livelihood—so much so that he had no house.

sentences.zh: 世或譏其多乞貸，亦隨復散之親故。

translations.literal: The world sometimes mocked him for much begging and borrowing, yet he at once gave it away to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: The world sometimes mocked him for much begging and borrowing, yet he at once gave it away to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 昉常歎曰：「知我亦以叔則，不知我亦以叔則。

translations.literal: Fang often sighed: "Those who know me know me by Uncle Ze; those who do not know me also know me by Uncle Ze."
translations.idiomatic: Fang often sighed, "Those who know me know me by Uncle Ze; those who do not know me also know me by Uncle Ze."

sentences.zh: 」昉墳籍無所不見，家雖貧，聚書至萬餘卷，率多異本。

translations.literal: Fang's library holdings he had seen everywhere—though the house was poor, books gathered to more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly rare editions.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had seen every book in the land—though his house was poor, his library held more than ten thousand scrolls, mostly rare editions.

sentences.zh: 昉卒後，高祖使學士賀縱共沈約勘其書目，官所無者，就昉家取之。

translations.literal: After Fang died, Gaozu had Academician He Zong together with Shen Yue collate his book catalog—what the office lacked, they took from Fang's house.
translations.idiomatic: After Fang died, Gaozu had Academician He Zong and Shen Yue collate his catalog—what the office lacked, they took from Fang's house.

sentences.zh: 昉所著文章數十萬言，盛行於世。

translations.literal: Fang's compositions ran to several hundred thousand words and flourished in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's writings ran to several hundred thousand words and flourished in the world.

sentences.zh: 初，昉立於士大夫間，多所汲引，有善己者則厚其聲名。

translations.literal: Early on Fang stood among the gentry and drew up many; if someone favored him he thickened that person's fame.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Fang stood among the gentry and drew many up; if someone favored him, he thickened that person's fame.

sentences.zh: 及卒，諸子皆幼，人罕贍卹之。

translations.literal: When he died his sons were all young; few came to support the bereaved.
translations.idiomatic: When he died his sons were all young; few came to support the bereaved.

sentences.zh: 平原劉孝標爲著論曰：

translations.literal: Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan wrote a discourse, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiaobiao of Pingyuan wrote a discourse, saying:

sentences.zh: 客問主人曰：「朱公叔《絕交論》，爲是乎？

translations.literal: The guest asked the host: "Was Zhu Gongshu's Discourse on Severing Friendship right?
translations.idiomatic: The guest asked the host, "Was Zhu Gongshu's Discourse on Severing Friendship right?

sentences.zh: 爲非乎？

translations.literal: Or wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: Or wrong?"

sentences.zh: 」主人曰：「客奚此之問？

translations.literal: The host said: "Guest, why this question?"
translations.idiomatic: The host said, "Guest, why this question?"

sentences.zh: 」客曰：「夫草蟲鳴則阜螽躍，雕虎嘯而清風起。

translations.literal: The guest said: "When the grass insect chirps, the mole cricket leaps; when the sculpted tiger roars, the clear wind rises.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "When the grass insect chirps, the mole cricket leaps; when the sculpted tiger roars, the clear wind rises.

sentences.zh: 故絪縕相感，霧湧雲蒸；

translations.literal: Thus kin-muffled mutual response—mist wells, clouds steam;
translations.idiomatic: Thus kin-muffled things answer one another—mist wells, clouds steam;

sentences.zh: 嚶鳴相召，星流電激。

translations.literal: crying calls crying summons—stars stream, lightning lashes.
translations.idiomatic: crying calls crying summons—stars stream, lightning lashes.

sentences.zh: 是以王陽登則貢公喜，罕生逝而國子悲。

translations.literal: Therefore when Wang Yang ascended, Lord Gong rejoiced; when Han Sheng departed, Guozi grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Wang Yang rose, Lord Gong rejoiced; when Han Sheng left, Guozi grieved.

sentences.zh: 且心同琴瑟，言鬱鬱於蘭茝，道叶膠漆，志婉孌於塤篪。

translations.literal: Moreover hearts matched like qin and se; words grew lush as orchids on iris; the Way bonded like glue and lacquer; wills entwined tender as xun and chi.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts were tuned like qin and se; words breathed orchid and iris; the Way clung like glue and lacquer; wills leaned together like paired pipes.

sentences.zh: 聖賢以此鏤金版而鐫盤盂，書玉牒而刻鐘鼎。

translations.literal: Sages for this carved gold plates and engraved bronze basins, wrote jade registers and cut bells and tripods.
translations.idiomatic: For this the sages cut gold plates, graved bronze vessels, wrote jade registers, and struck bells and tripods.

sentences.zh: 若匠人輟成風之妙巧，伯牙息流波之雅引。

translations.literal: As when a craftsman lays down the wind's subtle craft, or Boya ceases the flowing wave's elegant strain.
translations.idiomatic: As when the craftsman sets aside the wind's subtle craft, or Boya stills the flowing wave's elegant tune.

sentences.zh: 范、張款款於下泉，尹、班陶陶於永夕。

translations.literal: Fan and Zhang were earnest in the lower spring; Yin and Ban were at ease through the long night.
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Zhang kept faith in the underworld spring; Yin and Ban lingered easy through the long night.

sentences.zh: 駱驛縱橫，煙霏雨散，皆巧曆所不知，心計莫能測。

translations.literal: Galloping crosswise, mist veiling and rain scattering—all beyond the clever reckoner's ken, beyond the heart's measure.
translations.idiomatic: They galloped crosswise, veiled in mist, scattered in rain—beyond any clever reckoner, beyond any heart's measure.

sentences.zh: 而硃益州汨彜敘，越謨訓，捶直切，絕交遊，視黔首以鷹鸇，媲人倫於豺虎。

translations.literal: Yet Inspector Zhu of Yizhou penned his Yi narrative and Yue admonition, beat straight speech, severed all companionship, looked on the black-haired folk as hawk and kite, and matched human bonds to jackal and tiger.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu of Yizhou wrote his Yi narrative and Yue admonition, struck down straight speech, cut off all fellowship, saw common folk as hawks and kites, and weighed human ties against jackals and tigers.

sentences.zh: 蒙有猜焉，請辨其惑。」

translations.literal: I have doubts—please clear my confusion."
translations.idiomatic: I am puzzled—please resolve my doubt."

sentences.zh: 主人听然曰：「客所謂撫弦徽音，未達燥濕變響；

translations.literal: The host smiled and said, "What you call stroking the strings for pure tone has not reached how dryness and dampness change the sound;
translations.idiomatic: The host smiled and said, "You speak of stroking strings for pure tone, yet miss how dryness and dampness change the sound;

sentences.zh: 張羅沮澤，不睹鵠雁高飛。

translations.literal: spreading nets in the marsh and not seeing the swan and wild goose soar high."
translations.idiomatic: you spread nets in the marsh and never see swan and wild goose wheel high."

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人握金鏡，闡風烈，龍驤蠖屈，從道汙隆。

translations.literal: The sage holds the golden mirror and unfolds wind and merit; dragon rampant or silkworm bent, he follows the Way whether it sinks or rises.
translations.idiomatic: The sage holds the golden mirror, unfolds wind and merit; dragon rampant or silkworm bent, he follows the Way in rise or fall.

sentences.zh: 日月聯璧，歎亹亹之弘致；

translations.literal: Sun and moon like linked jades—he sighs at the tireless vast reach;
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon like linked jades—he sighs at tireless vast reach;

sentences.zh: 雲飛電薄，顯棣華之微旨。

translations.literal: clouds flying, lightning thin—he shows the subtle intent of flowering paulownia.
translations.idiomatic: clouds flying, lightning thin—he shows the subtle bloom of flowering paulownia.

sentences.zh: 若五音之變化，濟九成之妙曲。

translations.literal: Like the five tones' changes completing the nine accomplishments' subtle melody—
translations.idiomatic: Like the five tones' changes completing the nine accomplishments' subtle melody—

sentences.zh: 此朱生得玄珠於赤水，謨神睿而爲言。

translations.literal: this is Zhu gaining the dark pearl from Red Water, his admonition divine in wisdom made speech.
translations.idiomatic: this is Zhu winning the dark pearl from Red Water—divine wisdom turned into words.

sentences.zh: 至夫組織仁義，琢磨道德，歡其愉樂，恤其陵夷。

translations.literal: As for weaving benevolence and righteousness, polishing the moral Way, rejoicing in its pleasure, grieving its decline—
translations.idiomatic: As for weaving benevolence and righteousness, polishing the moral Way, rejoicing in its pleasure, grieving its ruin—

sentences.zh: 寄通靈臺之下，遺迹江湖之上，風雨急而不輟其音，霜雪零而不渝其色，斯賢達之素交，歷萬古而一遇。

translations.literal: lodging beneath the Spirit Terrace, leaving traces on rivers and lakes, wind and rain urgent yet never ceasing its tone, frost and snow fallen yet never staining its hue—such is the sage's plain friendship, met once in ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: lodging beneath the Spirit Terrace, leaving traces on rivers and lakes—wind and rain urgent yet the tone never breaks, frost and snow fallen yet the hue never stains—such is the sage's plain friendship, once in ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 逮叔世民訛，狙詐飇起，谿谷不能逾其險，鬼神無以究其變，競毛羽之輕，趨錐刀之末。

translations.literal: When the age turned corrupt and the people went astray, trickery and fraud rose like a gale; ravines and valleys could not hold back its peril, ghosts and spirits could not trace its shifts; all raced after feather-light gain and hurried to the knife's edge.
translations.idiomatic: When the age turned corrupt, trickery rose like a gale; ravines could not hold its peril, spirits could not trace its shifts; all raced after feather-light gain and hurried to the knife's edge.

sentences.zh: 於是素交盡，利交興，天下蚩蚩，鳥驚雷駭。

translations.literal: Then plain friendship perished and profit friendship arose; under heaven all seethed, birds startled and thunder crashed.
translations.idiomatic: Then plain friendship died and profit friendship rose; the world seethed—birds startled, thunder crashed.

sentences.zh: 然利交同源，派流則異，較言其略，有五術焉：

translations.literal: Yet profit friendship shares one source while its branches differ; compared in outline, there are five arts:
translations.idiomatic: Yet profit friendship shares one source with differing streams; in outline, five arts:

sentences.zh: 「若其寵鈞董、石，權壓梁、竇。

translations.literal: "Consider those who enjoy favor like Dong Xian and Shi Chong, whose power presses down Liang Ji and the Dou clan.
translations.idiomatic: "Consider those who enjoy favor like Dong Xian and Shi Chong, whose power crushes Liang Ji and the Dou clan.

sentences.zh: 雕刻百工，爐錘萬物，吐漱興雲雨，呼吸下霜露，九域聳其風塵，四海疊其燻灼。

translations.literal: They carve the hundred crafts, smelt the ten thousand things; exhaling they raise cloud and rain, inhaling they send down frost and dew; the nine regions shudder at their dust, the four seas pile their scorch.
translations.idiomatic: They carve the hundred crafts, smelt ten thousand things; breath out cloud and rain, breath in frost and dew; the nine regions shudder at their dust, the four seas pile their scorch.

sentences.zh: 靡不望影星奔，藉響川鶩，雞人始唱，鶴蓋成陰，高門旦開，流水接軫。

translations.literal: None fail to gaze at their star and run, borrow their echo and flock like geese on the stream; at the cock's first cry crane-canopies mass into shade, high gates open at dawn, flowing carriages link hub to hub.
translations.idiomatic: All gaze at their star and run, borrow their echo and flock like stream geese; at the cock's first cry crane-canopies mass into shade, high gates open at dawn, carriages link hub to hub.

sentences.zh: 皆願摩頂至踵，隳膽抽腸，約同要離焚妻子，誓徇荊卿湛七族。

translations.literal: All wish to grind the crown to the heel, crush the gall and draw the gut, pledge with Yao Li to burn wife and children, vow with Jing Ke to drown seven clans.
translations.idiomatic: All would grind crown to heel, crush gall and draw gut, pledge with Yao Li to burn wife and children, vow with Jing Ke to drown seven clans.

sentences.zh: 是曰勢交，其流一也。

translations.literal: This is power friendship—its current is the first.
translations.idiomatic: This is power friendship—the first current.

sentences.zh: 「富埒陶、白，貲巨程、羅，山擅銅陵，家藏金穴，出平原而聯騎，居里閈而鳴鐘。

translations.literal: "Wealth rivals Tao Zhugong and Bai Gui, assets exceed Cheng and Luo; mountains hold copper mines, houses hide gold pits; leaving the plain they link horses, dwelling in the lane they ring bells.
translations.idiomatic: "Wealth rivals Tao Zhugong and Bai Gui, assets exceed Cheng and Luo; mountains hold copper mines, houses hide gold pits; leaving the plain they link horses, in the lane they ring bells.

sentences.zh: 則有窮巷之賓，繩樞之士，冀宵燭之末光，邀潤屋之微澤，魚貫鳧踴，颯沓鱗萃，分雁鶩之稻粱，沾玉斝之餘瀝。

translations.literal: Then poor-lane guests and hemp-door scholars hope for the night candle's last gleam, beg the dripping-house's slight favor; fish strung, ducks hopping, rustling and scaling in heaps, they share the wild goose's grain and dip from the jade goblet's lees.
translations.idiomatic: Then poor-lane guests and hemp-door scholars hope for the night candle's last gleam, beg the dripping-house's slight favor; they string in like fish, hop like ducks, rustling in heaps, share the goose's grain, dip from the jade goblet's lees.

sentences.zh: 銜恩遇，進款誠，援青松以示心，指白水而旌信。

translations.literal: They bear favor received, advance earnest regard, offer the green pine to show the heart, point to white water to display faith.
translations.idiomatic: They bear favor, advance earnest regard, offer green pine to show the heart, point to white water to display faith.

sentences.zh: 是曰賄交，其流二也。

translations.literal: This is bribe friendship—its current is the second.
translations.idiomatic: This is bribe friendship—the second current.

sentences.zh: 「陸大夫燕喜西都，郭有道人倫東國，公卿貴其籍甚，搢紳羨其登仙。

translations.literal: "Grand Master Lu feasted in the western capital; Guo the Worthy ranked men in the eastern state; dukes and ministers prized his great fame, gentry envied his ascent to immortals.
translations.idiomatic: "Grand Master Lu feasted in the western capital; Guo the Worthy ranked men in the eastern state; nobles prized his fame, gentry envied his ascent among immortals.

sentences.zh: 加以顩頤蹙頞，涕唾流沫，騁黃馬之劇談，縱碧雞之雄辯，敘溫燠則寒谷成暄，論嚴枯則春叢零葉，飛沉出其顧指，榮辱定其一言。

translations.literal: Add a drawn chin and knitted brow, tears and spittle in foam, galloping yellow horses in fierce debate, loosing green cocks in bold argument—speak of warmth and the cold valley turns mild; speak of stern drought and spring thickets shed leaves; rise or fall follows a glance, glory or shame hangs on one word.
translations.idiomatic: Add drawn chin and knitted brow, tears and spittle flying, fierce debate on yellow horses, bold argument on green cocks—speak of warmth and the cold valley turns mild; speak of drought and spring thickets shed leaves; rise or fall follows a glance, glory or shame on one word.

sentences.zh: 於是弱冠王孫，綺紈公子，道不絓於通人，聲未遒於雲閣，攀其鱗翼，丐其餘論，附騏驥之髦端，軼歸鴻於碣石。

translations.literal: Then young lords in silk caps and brocade-clad heirs, whose Way never snags on the accomplished, whose voice never rings strong in the cloud pavilion, climb their scales and wings, beg their spare discourse, cling to the qiji's mane-tip, outpace the homing goose at Jieshi.
translations.idiomatic: Then young lords in silk caps and brocade heirs whose Way never snags on the accomplished, whose voice never rings in the cloud pavilion, climb their scales and wings, beg spare discourse, cling to the qiji's mane-tip, outpace the homing goose at Jieshi.

sentences.zh: 是曰談交，其流三也。

translations.literal: This is talk friendship—its current is the third.
translations.idiomatic: This is talk friendship—the third current.

sentences.zh: 「陽舒陰慘，生民大情，憂合歡離，品物恒性。

translations.literal: "Yang ease and yin grim are the great feelings of the living folk; sorrow joined and joy parted are the constant nature of things.
translations.idiomatic: "Yang ease and yin grim are the great feelings of living folk; sorrow joined and joy parted are things' constant nature.

sentences.zh: 故魚以泉涸而呴沫，鳥因將死而悲鳴。

translations.literal: So fish bubble when the spring dries, birds mourn as death nears.
translations.idiomatic: Fish bubble when the spring dries; birds mourn as death nears.

sentences.zh: 同病相憐，綴河上之悲曲；

translations.literal: Those who share affliction pity one another, stringing the river-bank's mournful tune;
translations.idiomatic: Those who share affliction pity one another, stringing the river-bank's mournful tune;

sentences.zh: 恐懼置懷，昭《谷風》之盛典。

translations.literal: fear placed in the breast displays the Gu Feng ode's grand ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: fear placed in the breast displays the Gu Feng ode's grand ceremony.

sentences.zh: 斯則斷金由於湫隘，刎頸起於苫蓋。

translations.literal: Thus broken gold comes from narrow straits, and severed necks rise from thatched mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus broken gold comes from narrow straits; severed necks rise from thatched mourning.

sentences.zh: 是以伍員濯溉於宰嚭，張王撫翼於陳相。

translations.literal: So Wu Yuan was washed by Zai Pi, Zhang and Wang spread wings at Chen's minister.
translations.idiomatic: So Wu Yuan was washed by Zai Pi; Zhang and Wang spread wings at Chen's minister.

sentences.zh: 是曰窮交，其流四也。

translations.literal: This is destitution friendship—its current is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: This is destitution friendship—the fourth current.

sentences.zh: 「馳鶩之俗，澆薄之倫，無不操權衡，秉纖纊。

translations.literal: "In the rushing-grouse age, the thin and shallow sort, none fails to hold the balance-scale and grasp the gossamer.
translations.idiomatic: "In the rushing-grouse age, the thin and shallow sort—none fails to hold the balance-scale and grasp gossamer.

sentences.zh: 衡所以揣其輕重，纊所以屬其鼻息。

translations.literal: The scale weighs their heaviness and lightness; the gossamer tests their breath.
translations.idiomatic: The scale weighs heaviness and lightness; the gossamer tests their breath.

sentences.zh: 若衡不能舉，纊不能飛，雖顏、冉龍翰鳳＜芻鳥＞，曾、史，蘭熏雪白，舒、向金玉，淵海卿、雲，黼黻河漢，視若遊塵。

translations.literal: If the scale cannot lift and the gossamer cannot fly, though Yan and Ran had dragon sinews and phoenix pinions, Zeng and Shi orchid scent and snow-white, Shu and Xiang jade and gold, Yuan and Yun abyss-sea, He and Han brocade and Milky Way—they are seen as wandering dust.
translations.idiomatic: If the scale cannot lift and the gossamer cannot fly, though Yan and Ran had dragon sinews and phoenix pinions, Zeng and Shi orchid scent and snow-white, Shu and Xiang jade and gold, Yuan and Yun abyss-sea, He and Han brocade and Milky Way—they are wandering dust.

sentences.zh: 遇同土梗，莫肯費其半菽，罕有落其一毛。

translations.literal: Met as clay puppets, none will spend half a bean; rarely does one lose a single hair.
translations.idiomatic: Met as clay puppets, none spends half a bean; rarely does one lose a single hair.

sentences.zh: 若衡重錙銖，纊微彯撇，雖共工之蒐慝，驩兜之掩義，南荊之跋扈，東陵之巨猾，皆爲匍匐委蛇，折枝舐痔，金膏翠羽將其意，脂韋便辟導其誠。

translations.literal: If the scale weighs heavy as a cash-weight and the gossamer stirs the slightest breath, though Gong Gong's search for evil, Huan Dou's masking of righteousness, the southern Jing's arrogance, the eastern mound's great knavery—all crawl and writhe, break branches and lick hemorrhoids; gold paste and kingfisher plumes suit their intent, grease and rush smooth the way to their sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: If the scale weighs heavy as a cash-weight and the gossamer stirs the slightest breath, though Gong Gong's evil, Huan Dou's masked righteousness, southern Jing's arrogance, eastern mound's great knavery—all crawl and writhe, break branches and lick hemorrhoids; gold paste and kingfisher plumes suit their intent, grease and rush smooth their sincerity.

sentences.zh: 故輪蓋所遊，必非夷、惠之室；

translations.literal: Thus wherever carriage wheels travel, it cannot be Bo Yi and Hui Shi's house;
translations.idiomatic: Thus wherever carriage wheels travel, it is not Bo Yi and Hui Shi's house;

sentences.zh: 苞苴所入，實行張、霍之家。

translations.literal: wherever bribes enter, it is truly Zhang and Huo's home.
translations.idiomatic: wherever bribes enter, it is truly Zhang and Huo's home.

sentences.zh: 謀而後動，芒毫寡忒。

translations.literal: They plot before they act; not a hair's error.
translations.idiomatic: They plot before they act—not a hair's error.

sentences.zh: 是曰量交，其流五也。

translations.literal: This is measure friendship—its current is the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: This is measure friendship—the fifth current.

sentences.zh: 「凡斯五交，義同賈鬻，故桓譚譬之於闤闠，林回喻之於甘醴。

translations.literal: "All these five friendships share the righteousness of buying and selling; thus Huan Tan compared them to the market stall, Lin Hui to sweet wine.
translations.idiomatic: "All five friendships share the righteousness of buying and selling; Huan Tan compared them to the market stall, Lin Hui to sweet wine.

sentences.zh: 夫寒暑遞進，盛衰相襲，或前榮而後瘁，或始富而終貧，或初存而末亡，或古約而今泰，循環翻覆，迅若波瀾。

translations.literal: Cold and heat advance in turn, flourishing and decline succeed each other; some glory first then wither, some rich at first then poor, some whole at first then perish, some austere in old days and opulent now—turning in cycles, swift as waves.
translations.idiomatic: Cold and heat advance in turn, flourishing and decline succeed; some glory first then wither, some rich then poor, some whole then perish, some austere once and opulent now—turning in cycles, swift as waves.

sentences.zh: 此則徇利之情未嘗異，變化之道不得一。

translations.literal: Thus the feeling that runs after profit has never differed, yet the Way of change cannot be one.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the feeling that runs after profit never differs, yet the Way of change cannot be one.

sentences.zh: 由是觀之，張、陳所以凶終，蕭、朱所以隙末，斷焉可知矣。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, why Zhang and Chen met violent ends, why Xiao and Zhu found rifts at the close—it can be known at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, why Zhang and Chen met violent ends, why Xiao and Zhu found rifts at the close—clear at a glance.

sentences.zh: 而翟公方規規然勒門以箴客，何所見之晚乎？

translations.literal: Yet Duke Zhai stood primly at his gate to admonish guests—how late his sight!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Duke Zhai stood primly at his gate to admonish guests—how late his sight!

sentences.zh: 「然因此五交，是生三釁：敗德殄義，禽獸相若，一釁也；

translations.literal: "Yet from these five friendships three faults arise: ruining virtue and extinguishing righteousness, beasts matching beasts—the first fault;
translations.idiomatic: "Yet from these five friendships three faults arise: ruining virtue and extinguishing righteousness, beasts matching beasts—the first fault;

sentences.zh: 難固易攜，讎訟所聚，二釁也；

translations.literal: hard to bind, easy to break, quarrels and lawsuits gather—the second fault;
translations.idiomatic: hard to bind, easy to break, quarrels and lawsuits gather—the second fault;

sentences.zh: 名陷饕餮，貞介所羞，三釁也。

translations.literal: name fallen to gluttony, integrity shamed—the third fault.
translations.idiomatic: name fallen to gluttony, integrity shamed—the third fault.

sentences.zh: 古人知三釁之爲梗，懼五交之速尤。

translations.literal: The ancients knew the three faults were obstruction and feared the five friendships' swift blame.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients knew the three faults obstructed and feared the five friendships' swift blame.

sentences.zh: 故王丹威子以檟楚，朱穆昌言而示絕，有旨哉！

translations.literal: Thus Wang Dan chastised his son with the mulberry rod; Zhu Mu spoke plainly to show severance—how apt!
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wang Dan chastised his son with the mulberry rod; Zhu Mu spoke plainly to show severance—how apt!

sentences.zh: 「近世有樂安任昉，海內髦傑，早綰銀黃，夙招民譽。

translations.literal: "In recent times there was Ren Fang of Le'an, a crest of the realm, who early bound the silver seal and long drew the people's praise.
translations.idiomatic: "In recent times Ren Fang of Le'an, a crest of the realm, early bound the silver seal and long drew the people's praise.

sentences.zh: 遒文麗藻，方駕曹、王；

translations.literal: His forceful prose and gorgeous pattern rivaled Cao and Wang;
translations.idiomatic: His forceful prose and gorgeous pattern rivaled Cao and Wang;

sentences.zh: 英特俊邁，聯衡許、郭。

translations.literal: outstanding and far-reaching, he matched Xu and Guo in the scales.
translations.idiomatic: outstanding and far-reaching, he matched Xu and Guo in the scales.

sentences.zh: 類田文之愛客，同鄭莊之好賢。

translations.literal: Like Lord Mengchang he loved guests, like Zheng Zhuang he delighted in the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Like Lord Mengchang he loved guests; like Zheng Zhuang he delighted in the worthy.

sentences.zh: 見一善則盱衡扼腕，遇一才則揚眉抵掌。

translations.literal: See one good deed and he threw back his head and clenched his wrist; meet one talent and he arched his brow and clapped his palm.
translations.idiomatic: See one good deed and he threw back his head and clenched his wrist; meet one talent and he arched his brow and clapped his palm.

sentences.zh: 雌黃出其脣吻，硃紫由其月旦。

translations.literal: Orpiment and cinnabar came from his lips; scarlet and purple from his monthly rating.
translations.idiomatic: Orpiment and cinnabar came from his lips; scarlet and purple from his monthly rating.

sentences.zh: 於是冠蓋輻湊，衣裳雲合，輜軿擊轊，坐客恒滿。

translations.literal: Then carriage canopies converged like wheel spokes, robes clouded together, curtained coaches clattered at the hubs, and seated guests were always full.
translations.idiomatic: Carriage canopies converged like wheel spokes, robes clouded together, curtained coaches clattered at the hubs, seated guests always full.

sentences.zh: 蹈其閫閾，若升闕里之堂；

translations.literal: Tread his threshold as if ascending the Hall of the Confucian temple;
translations.idiomatic: Tread his threshold as if ascending the Hall of the Confucian temple;

sentences.zh: 入其奧隅，謂登龍門之阪。

translations.literal: enter his inner chambers as if climbing the Dragon Gate's slope.
translations.idiomatic: enter his inner chambers as if climbing the Dragon Gate's slope.

sentences.zh: 至於顧盼增其倍價，剪拂使其長鳴，彯組雲臺者摩肩，趨走丹墀者疊迹。

translations.literal: A single glance from him doubled a man's worth; a stroke along the mane made the horse cry out into the long wind. Ribbons from the cloud platform crowded shoulder to shoulder; runners on the cinnabar steps left their tracks in layers.
translations.idiomatic: One glance from him doubled a man's worth; one comb-stroke along the mane made the horse cry long. Cloud-platform ribbons pressed shoulder to shoulder; runners on the cinnabar steps left tracks in layers.

sentences.zh: 莫不締恩狎，結綢繆，想惠、莊之清塵，庶羊、左之徽烈。
